requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The clear port operation IS the port operation that empties incoming port queues.
requirements.original: The clear port operation empties incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The clear port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." clear.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." clear

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `clear` operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port.
requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: When used with `all port`, the `clear` operation removes the contents of the incoming queues of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.
requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port queue is already empty
requirements.canonical: If a port queue is already empty, the `clear` operation SHALL have no action on that port.
requirements.original: If a port queue is already empty then this operation shall have no action on that port.

requirements.subject: ent:clear-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The clear port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `clear`.
requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Clear port; Col2: clear

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The start port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `start`.
requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Start port; Col2: start

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `stop`.
requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Stop port; Col2: stop

requirements.subject: ent:halt-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The halt port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `halt`.
requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Halt port; Col2: halt

requirements.subject: ent:checkstate-operation
requirements.canonical: The check the state of a port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `checkstate`.
requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Check the state of a port; Col2: checkstate

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `clear` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `start` port operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The start operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The start port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." start.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." start

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation clears the incoming queue of the named port.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation starts listening for traffic over the port.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.subject: ent:sending-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been started
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, after the `start` operation sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` MAY be performed at that port.
requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. are also allowed to be performed at that port.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: All ports of a test component SHALL be started implicitly when the component is created.
requirements.original: By default, all ports of a component shall be started implicitly when a component is created.

requirements.subject: ent:start-port-operation
requirements.canonical: A `start` operation applied to an unstopped port restarts the port by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
requirements.original: The start port operation will cause unstopped ports to be restarted by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.

readings: A `start` operation applied to an already started port restarts it by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
A `start` operation applied to a port that is not in the stopped state (started or halted) clears its incoming queue.
ambiguity.issue: 'unstopped ports' is not a defined port state; chose the reading that covers every non-stopped port (started or halted), consistent with NOTE 3 of 22.5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `start` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disables sending operations at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disallows receiving operations to match at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." stop.
requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." stop

requirements.subject: ent:stop-port-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `stop` operation causes listening at the named port to cease.
requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive and getcall, the stop operation causes listening at the named port to cease.

requirements.subject: ent:sending-operation
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been stopped
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` SHALL NOT be performed at that port after a `stop` operation.
requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then stop port disallows the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: When a port is stopped, all receiving operations at that port performed before the `stop` operation SHALL be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.
requirements.original: To cease listening at the port means that all receiving operations defined before the stop operation shall be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.

readings: Receiving operations already executed (successfully matched) before the `stop` operation are completed, i.e. their effects (e.g. value redirections) take place.
Receiving operations that appear textually before the `stop` operation in the behaviour are performed completely before the port is suspended.
ambiguity.issue: 'defined before the stop operation' is unclear: executed before in time or written before in the code; chose the temporal execution reading.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `stop` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
